a-fortiori.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Latin (Mathematical)).

acute-angle.definition: Book I: 12. An acute angle is an angle less than a right angle.

acute-angled-cone.definition: Book XI: And, if the straight line which remains fixed be equal to the remaining side about the right angle which is carried round, the cone will be right-angled; if less, obtuse-angled; and if greater, acute-angled.

acute-angled-triangle.definition: Book I: 21. Further, of trilateral figures, a right-angled triangle is that which has a right angle, an obtuse-angled triangle that which has an obtuse angle, and an acute-angled triangle that which has its three angles acute.

ad-infinitum.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Latin (Mathematical)).

adiaireton.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Greek).

alternando.translation: Alternate ratio (taking antecedent to antecedent as consequent to consequent)
alternando.definition: Book V, Def. 12: If A : B = C : D, then alternando A : C = B : D (proved in V.16).

amblygonion.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Greek).

analogia.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Greek).

angle.definition: The inclination to one another of two lines in a plane which meet one another and do not lie in a straight line (classified by Aristotle, Syrianus, and Proclus under quality, quantity, or relation).

angle-in-segment.definition: Book III: 8. An angle in a segment is the angle which, when a point is taken on the circumference of the segment and straight lines are joined from it to the extremities of the straight line which is the base of the segment, is contained by the straight lines so joined.

angle-of-contact.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Mathematical Term).

angle-of-segment.definition: Book III: 7. An angle of a segment is that contained by a straight line and a circumference of a circle.

annex.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Greek).

antanairesis.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Greek).

anthyphairesis.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Greek).

antistrophe.definition: Heath Greek Index: ἀντιστροφή — conversion 256–7: leading variety, ἡ προηγουμένη or ἡ κυρίως, ibid.

apagoge.definition: Heath Greek Index: ἀπαγωγή — reduction 135: εἰς τὸ ἀδύνατον 136

apodeixis.definition: The fifth formal division of a Euclidean proposition, drawing the deductive chain of assertions from the hypotheses, constructions, axioms, and prior propositions.

apotome.definition: Book X.73: The irrational remainder when a rational straight line commensurable in square only with the whole is subtracted from a rational straight line; classified into six species in Book X Defs. III.

arrhetos.definition: Heath Greek Index: ἄρρητος — irrational: of λόγος 137: of diameter (diagonal) 399

asymptotos.definition: Heath Greek Index: ἀσύμπτωτος — not-meeting, non-secant, asymptotic 40, 161, 203

atomoi-grammai.definition: Heath Greek Index: ἄτομοι γραμμαί — "indivisible lines" 268

axis-of-cone.definition: Book XI: 19. The axis of the cone is the straight line which remains fixed and about which the triangle is turned.

axis-of-cylinder.definition: Book XI: 22. The axis of the cylinder is the straight line which remains fixed and about which the parallelogram is turned.

axis-of-sphere.definition: Book XI: 15. The axis of the sphere is the straight line which remains fixed and about which the semicircle is turned.

base-of-cone.definition: Book XI: 20. And the base is the circle described by the straight line which is carried round.

base-of-segment.definition: Book III: 8. An angle in a segment is the angle which, when a point is taken on the circumference of the segment and straight lines are joined from it to the extremities of the straight line which is the base of the segment, is contained by the straight lines so joined.

bases-of-cylinder.definition: Book XI: 23. And the bases are the circles described by the two sides opposite to one another which are carried round.

binomial.definition: Book X.36: The irrational sum of two rational straight lines commensurable in square only; classified into six species in Book X Defs. II.

boundary.definition: Book I: 13. A boundary is that which is an extremity of anything.

centre.headword: Centre of the circle (κέντρον τοῦ κύκλου)
centre.translation: Κέντρον δὲ τοῦ κύκλου τὸ σημεῖον καλεῖται
centre.definition: Book I, Def. 16: 'And the point is called the centre of the circle.'

centre-of-sphere.definition: Book XI: 16. The centre of the sphere is the same as that of the semicircle.

circle.translation: Κύκλος ἐστὶ σχῆμα ἐπίπεδον ὑπὸ μιᾶς γραμμῆς περιεχόμενον...
circle.definition: Book I, Def. 15: 'A circle is a plane figure contained by one line such that all the straight lines falling upon it from one point among those lying within the figure are equal to one another.'

circle-inscribed-in-figure.definition: Book IV: 5. Similarly a circle is said to be inscribed in a figure when the circumference of the circle touches each side of the figure in which it is inscribed.

circles-touching.definition: Book III: 3. **Circles** are said to touch one another which, meeting one another, do not cut one another.

circumscribed-about-circle.definition: Book IV: 4. A rectilineal figure is said to be circumscribed about a circle, when each side of the circumscribed figure touches the circumference of the circle.

circumscribed-about-figure.definition: Book IV: 2. Similarly a figure is said to be circumscribed about a figure when the respective sides of the circumscribed figure pass through the respective angles of that about which it is circumscribed.

commensurable.translation: Σύμμετρα μεγέθη λέγεται τὰ τῷ αὐτῷ μέτρῳ μετρούμενα
commensurable.definition: Book X, Def. 1: 'Those magnitudes are said to be commensurable which are measured by the same measure, and those incommensurable which cannot have any common measure.'

commensurable-in-length.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Mathematical Term).

commensurable-in-square.definition: Book X: 2. Straight lines are commensurable in square when the squares on them are measured by the same area, and incommensurable in square when the squares on them cannot possibly have any area as a common measure.

commensurable-in-square-only.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Mathematical Term).

componendo.translation: Composition of a ratio (antecedent + consequent to consequent)
componendo.definition: Book V, Def. 14: If A : B = C : D, then componendo (A + B) : B = (C + D) : D (proved in V.18).

composite-number.definition: Book VII: 13. A composite number is that which is measured by some number.

composite-to-one-another.definition: Book VII: 14. Numbers composite to one another are those which are measured by some number as a common measure.

compound-ratio.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Mathematical Term).

cone.definition: Book XI: 18. When, one side of those about the right angle in a right-angled triangle remaining fixed, the triangle is carried round and restored again to the same position from which it began to be moved, the figure so comprehended is a cone.

contained-rectangle.definition: Book II: 1. Any rectangular parallelogram is said to be contained by the two straight lines containing the right angle.

convertendo.translation: Conversion of a ratio (antecedent to antecedent − consequent)
convertendo.definition: Book V, Def. 16: If A : B = C : D, then convertendo A : (A − B) = C : (C − D) (V.19 Porism).

corresponding-magnitudes.definition: Book V: 11. The term corresponding magnitudes is used of antecedents in relation to antecedents, and of consequents in relation to consequents.

cube.definition: Book XI: 25. A cube is a solid figure contained by six equal squares.

cube-number.definition: Book VII: 19. And a cube is equal multiplied by equal and again by equal, or a number which is contained by three equal numbers.

cylinder.definition: Book XI: 21. When, one side of those about the right angle in a rectangular parallelogram remaining fixed, the parallelogram is carried round and restored again to the same position from which it began to be moved, the figure so comprehended is a cylinder.

diameter.headword: Diameter of the circle (διάμετρος τοῦ κύκλου)
diameter.translation: Διάμετρος δὲ τοῦ κύκλου ἐστὶν εὐθεῖά τις διὰ τοῦ κέντρου ἠγμένη...
diameter.definition: Book I, Def. 17: 'A diameter of the circle is any straight line drawn through the centre and terminated in both directions by the circumference of the circle, and such a straight line also bisects the circle.'

diameter-of-sphere.definition: Book XI: 17. A diameter of the sphere is any straight line drawn through the centre and terminated in both directions by the surface of the sphere.

diastema.definition: Heath Greek Index: διάστημα — distance 166, 167, 207: (of radius of circle) 199: (of an angle) = divergence 176–7

dimensions.definition: Heath Greek Index: διαστάσεις — almost = dimensions 157, 158

diorismos.definition: Either (1) the third formal division of a proposition restating the goal in terms of the particular figure, or (2) the determination of the limits/conditions under which a problem admits of a solution.

dodecahedron.definition: Book XI: 28. A dodecahedron is a solid figure contained by twelve equal, equilateral, and equiangular pentagons.

dokis.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Greek).

duplicate-ratio.definition: Book V: 9. When three magnitudes are proportional, the first is said to have to the third the duplicate ratio of that which it has to the second.

dynameis.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Greek).

dynamene.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Greek).

dynamis.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Greek).

dynasthai.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Greek).

eis-to-adynaton.translation: Reduction to the impossible (reductio ad absurdum)
eis-to-adynaton.definition: Indirect demonstration proving a proposition by showing that its contradiction leads to an impossibility.

ekthesis.definition: The second formal division of a Euclidean proposition, instantiating the given data in a concrete geometric figure with lettered elements.

elleipsis.definition: Heath Greek Index: ἔλλειψις — falling-short (with reference to application of areas) 36, 343–5, 383–4

ephaptesthai.definition: Heath Greek Index: ἐφάπτεσθαι — to touch 57

epharmozein.definition: Heath Greek Index: ἐφαρμόζειν — to coincide, ἐφαρμόζεσθαι, to be applied to 168, 224–5, 249

epipedon.definition: Heath Greek Index: ἐπίπεδον — plane in Euclid, used for surface also in Plato and Aristotle 169

equal-and-similar-solid-figures.definition: Book XI: 10. Equal and similar solid figures are those contained by similar planes equal in multitude and in magnitude.

equal-circles.definition: Book III: 1. Equal circles are those the diameters of which are equal, or the radii of which are equal.

equal-multiplied-by-equal.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Greek).

equally-distant-from-centre.definition: Book III: 4. In a circle straight lines are said to be equally distant from the centre when the perpendiculars drawn to them from the centre are equal.

equilateral-triangle.definition: Book I: 20. Of trilateral figures, an equilateral triangle is that which has its three sides equal, an isosceles triangle that which has two of its sides alone equal, and a scalene triangle that which has its three sides unequal.

even-number.definition: Book VII: 6. An even number is that which is divisible into two equal parts.

even-times-even-number.definition: Book VII: 8. An even-times even number is that which is measured by an even number according to an even number.

even-times-odd-number.definition: Book VII: 9. An even-times odd number is that which is measured by an even number according to an odd number.

ex-aequali.translation: Ratio ex aequali (taking extreme to extreme across ordered series of ratios)
ex-aequali.definition: Book V, Def. 17: If A : B = D : E and B : C = E : F, then ex aequali A : C = D : F (proved in V.22; perturbed proportion in V.23).

extended.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Greek).

extreme-and-mean-ratio.headword: Extreme and mean ratio (ἄκρος καὶ μέσος λόγος)
extreme-and-mean-ratio.definition: Book VI, Def. 3: 'A straight line is said to have been cut in extreme and mean ratio when, as the whole line is to the greater segment, so is the greater to the less.' (Constructed in II.11 and VI.30; applied to the pentagon, icosahedron, and dodecahedron in Book XIII).

occurrences.display: A straight line is said to have been cut in extreme and mean ratio

extremity.definition: Book I: 3. The extremities of a line are points.

fifth-apotome.definition: Book X: **5.** if the annex be so commensurable, a fifth ;

fifth-binomial.definition: Book X: 5. if the lesser, a fifth binomial;

figure.definition: Book I: 14. A figure is that which is contained by any boundary or boundaries.

first-apotome.definition: Book X: **1.** Given a rational straight line and an apotome, if the square on the whole be greater than the square on the annex by the square on a straight line commensurable in length with the whole, and the whole be commensurable in length with the rational straight line set out, let the apotome be called a first apotome.

first-apotome-of-a-medial-straight-line.translation: first apotome of a medial straight line
first-apotome-of-a-medial-straight-line.definition: Book X: | And let it be called a first apotome of a medial straight line.

occurrences.display: first apotome of a medial straight line
first apotome of a medial straight line
first apotome of a medial straight line
first apotome of a medial straight line
first apotome of a medial straight line
first apotome of a medial straight line

first-bimedial.definition: Book X: If two medial straight lines commensurable in square only and containing a rational rectangle be added together, the whole is irrational; and let it be called a first bimedial straight line.

first-binomial.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Mathematical Term).

first-binomial-straight-line.definition: Book X: **1.** Given a rational straight line and a binomial, divided into its terms, such that the square on the greater term is greater than the square on the lesser by the square on a straight line commensurable in length with the greater, then, if the greater term be commensurable in length with the rational straight line set out, let the whole be called a first binomial straight line;

fitted-into-circle.definition: Book IV: 7. A straight line is said to be fitted into a circle when its extremities are on the circumference of the circle.

fourth-apotome.definition: Book X: **4.** Again, if the square on the whole be greater than the square on the annex by the square on a straight line incommensurable with the whole, then, if the whole be com- mensurable in length with the rational straight line set out, let the apotome be called a fourth apotome ;

fourth-binomial.definition: Book X: 4. Again, if the square on the greater term be greater than the square on the lesser by the square on a straight line incommensurable in length with the greater, then, if the greater term be commensurable in length with the rational straight line set out, let the whole be called a fourth binomial;

gamelion-diagramma.definition: Heath Greek Index: γαμήλιον διάγραμμα — "Figure of Marriage" (Plutarch), term for Pythagorean triangle (3, 4, 5), 417

gnomon.definition: Book II, Def. 2: 'In any parallelogrammic area let any one whatever of the parallelograms about its diameter with the two complements be called a gnomon.'

golden-section.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Mathematical Term).

greater-distance-from-centre.definition: Book III: 5. And that straight line is said to be at a greater distance on which the greater perpendicular falls.

greater-ratio.definition: Book V: 7. When, of the equimultiples, the multiple of the first magnitude exceeds the multiple of the second, but the multiple of the third does not exceed the multiple of the fourth, then the first is said to have a greater ratio to the second than the third has to the fourth.

have-a-ratio.definition: Book V: 4. Magnitudes are said to have a ratio to one another which are capable, when multiplied, of exceeding one another.

hegoumenon.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Greek).

height.definition: Book VI: 4. The height of any figure is the perpendicular drawn from the vertex to the base.

hepomenon.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Greek).

heteromekes-arithmos.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Greek).

hippou-pede.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Greek).

homoiomeres.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Greek).

hoper-edei-deixai.translation: Being what it was required to prove (Quod erat demonstrandum)
hoper-edei-deixai.definition: Euclid's canonical closing formula for every theorem.

hoper-edei-poiesai.translation: Being what it was required to do (Quod erat faciendum)
hoper-edei-poiesai.definition: Euclid's canonical closing formula for every construction problem.

hornlike-angle.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Greek).

horos.definition: A definition delimiting the meaning of a geometric or arithmetic term.

hyperbole.definition: Heath Greek Index: ὑπερβολή — exceeding, with reference to method of application of areas 36, 343–5, 386–7

icosahedron.definition: Book XI: 27. An icosahedron is a solid figure contained by twenty equal and equilateral triangles.

in-length.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Greek).

in-square.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Greek).

in-the-same-ratio.definition: Book V: 5. Magnitudes are said to be in the same ratio, the first to the second and the third to the fourth, when, if any equimultiples whatever be taken of the first and third, and any equimultiples whatever of the second and fourth, the former equimultiples alike exceed, are alike equal to, or alike fall short of, the latter equimultiples respectively taken in corresponding order.

inclination-of-line-to-plane.headword: inclination of a straight line to a plane
inclination-of-line-to-plane.definition: Book XI: 5. The inclination of a straight line to a plane is, assuming a perpendicular drawn from the extremity of the straight line which is elevated above the plane to the plane, and a straight line joined from the point thus arising to the extremity of the straight line which is in the plane, the angle contained by the straight line so drawn and the straight line standing up.

occurrences.display: inclination of a straight line to a plane

inclination-of-plane-to-plane.headword: inclination of a plane to a plane
inclination-of-plane-to-plane.definition: Book XI: 6. The inclination of a plane to a plane is the acute angle contained by the straight lines drawn at right angles to the common section at the same point, one in each of the planes.

occurrences.display: inclination of a plane to a plane

incommensurable.definition: Book X, Def. 1: Magnitudes which cannot have any common measure.

incommensurable-in-length.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Mathematical Term).

incommensurable-in-square.definition: Book X: 2. Straight lines are commensurable in square when the squares on them are measured by the same area, and incommensurable in square when the squares on them cannot possibly have any area as a common measure.

inscribed-in-circle.definition: Book IV: 3. A rectilineal figure is said to be inscribed in a circle when each angle of the inscribed figure lies on the circumference of the circle.

inscribed-in-rectilineal-figure.definition: Book IV: 1. A rectilineal figure is said to be inscribed in a rectilineal figure when the respective angles of the inscribed figure lie on the respective sides of that in which it is inscribed.

invertendo.definition: Book V, Def. 13: If A : B = C : D, then invertendo B : A = D : C (V.7 Porism).

irrational.definition: Book X, Def. 3: A straight line incommensurable both in length and in square with the assigned rational straight line.

irrational-diameter-of-five.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Greek).

isakis.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Greek).

isopleuron.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Greek).

isosceles-triangle.definition: Book I: 20. Of trilateral figures, an equilateral triangle is that which has its three sides equal, an isosceles triangle that which has two of its sides alone equal, and a scalene triangle that which has its three sides unequal.

kataskeue.definition: The fourth formal division of a Euclidean proposition, adding auxiliary lines and circles justified by the Postulates or prior problems.

kathetos.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Greek).

keratoeides.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Greek).

koinai-doxai.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Greek).

koinai-ennoiai.definition: Euclid's title for universal, self-evident axioms shared across sciences (called τὰ κοινά or ἀξιώματα by Aristotle).

koryphe.definition: Heath Greek Index: κορυφή — vertex: κατὰ κορυφήν, vertical (angles) 278

line.definition: Book I, Def. 2: 'A line is breadthless length.' Book I, Def. 3: 'The extremities of a line are points.'

major.definition: Book X: If two straight lines incommensurable in square which make the sum of the squares on them rational, but the rectangle contained by them medial, be added together, the whole straight line is irrational : and let it be called major.

mathemata.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Greek).

medial.definition: Book X.21: The side of an irrational rectangle contained by two rational straight lines commensurable in square only (equivalent to ⁴√k · ρ).

megethos.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Greek).

menoeides.definition: Heath Greek Index: μηνοειδής — lune-like (of angle) 26, 201: τὸ μηνοειδὲς (σχῆμα), lune 187

mesotes.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Greek).

method.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Greek).

method-of-exhaustion.translation: Exhaustion by inscribed/circumscribed polygons or polyhedra (Eudoxus & Archimedes)
method-of-exhaustion.definition: Rigorous Greek limiting method grounded in Book X.1 (and Book V Def. 4) avoiding actual infinitesimals via double reductio ad absurdum.

minor.definition: Book X: And let it be called minor. Q. E. D.

monas-proslabousa-thesin.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Greek).

monostrophos-helix.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Greek).

multilateral.definition: Book I: 19. Rectilineal figures are those which are contained by straight lines, trilateral figures being those contained by three, quadrilateral those contained by four, and multilateral those contained by more than four straight lines.

multiple.definition: Book V: 2. The greater is a multiple of the less when it is measured by the less.

multiply.definition: Book VII: 15. A number is said to multiply a number when that which is multiplied is added to itself as many times as there are units in the other, and thus some number is produced.

mutatis-mutandis.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Latin (Mathematical)).

neuseis.definition: Heath Greek Index: νεύσεις — inclinations, a class of problems 150–1: νεύειν, to verge 118, 150

number.translation: Ἀριθμὸς δὲ τὸ ἐκ μονάδων συγκείμενον πλῆθος
number.definition: Book VII, Def. 2: 'A number is a multitude composed of units.'

oblong.definition: Book I: 22. Of quadrilateral figures, a square is that which is both equilateral and right-angled ; an oblong that which is right-angled but not equilateral ; a rhombus that which is equilateral but not right-angled ; and a rhomboid that which has its opposite sides and angles equal to one another but is neither equilateral nor right-angled. And let quadrilaterals other than these be called trapezia.

obtuse-angle.definition: Book I: 11. An obtuse angle is an angle greater than a right angle.

obtuse-angled-cone.definition: Book XI: And, if the straight line which remains fixed be equal to the remaining side about the right angle which is carried round, the cone will be right-angled; if less, obtuse-angled; and if greater, acute-angled.

obtuse-angled-triangle.definition: Book I: 21. Further, of trilateral figures, a right-angled triangle is that which has a right angle, an obtuse-angled triangle that which has an obtuse angle, and an acute-angled triangle that which has its three angles acute.

octahedron.definition: Book XI: 26. An octahedron is a solid figure contained by eight equal and equilateral triangles.

odd-number.definition: Book VII: 7. An odd number is that which is not divisible into two equal parts, or that which differs by an unit from an even number.

odd-times-even-number.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Mathematical Term).

odd-times-odd-number.definition: Book VII: 10. An odd-times odd number is that which is measured by an odd number according to an odd number.

orthogonion.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Greek).

oxygonion.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Greek).

parabole.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Greek).

parabole-ton-chorion.definition: The Pythagorean geometric-algebraic method (Book I.44–45, Book II, Book VI.27–29) of applying a parallelogram equal to a given area along a given straight line—either exactly (παραβολή), in defect (ἔλλειψις), or in excess (ὑπερβολή).

paradoxos-topos.definition: Heath Greek Index: παράδοξος τόπος — ὁ, "the Treasury of Paradoxes" 329

parallel-planes.definition: Book XI: 8. Parallel planes are those which do not meet.

parallel-straight-lines.translation: Παράλληλοί εἰσιν εὐθεῖαι, αἵτινες ἐν τῷ αὐτῷ ἐπιπέδῳ οὖσαι καὶ ἐκβαλλόμεναι εἰς ἄπειρον ἐφ' ἑκάτερα τὰ μέρη ἐπὶ μηδέτερα συμπίπτουσιν ἀλλήλαις
parallel-straight-lines.definition: Book I, Def. 23: 'Parallel straight lines are straight lines which, being in the same plane and being produced indefinitely in both directions, do not meet one another in either direction.'

parallelepiped.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Greek).

parallelogrammon.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Greek).

parapleroma.definition: Heath Greek Index: παραπλήρωμα — complement, q.v.

part-aliquot.definition: Book V: 1. A magnitude is a part of a magnitude, the less of the greater, when it measures the greater.

parts-non-aliquot.definition: Book VII: 4. but parts when it does not measure it.

pelikotes.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Greek).

perainousa-posotes.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Greek).

peras.definition: Heath Greek Index: πέρας — extremity 165, 182: πέρας συγκλεῖον (Posidonius' definition of figure) 183

peras-synkleion.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Greek).

perfect-number.translation: Τέλειος ἀριθμός ἐστιν ὁ τοῖς ἑαυτοῦ μέρεσιν ἴσος ὤν
perfect-number.definition: Book VII, Def. 22: 'A perfect number is that which is equal to its own parts.' (Constructed from prime sums of powers of two in IX.36).

perpendicular.definition: Book I: 10. When a straight line set up on a straight line makes the adjacent angles equal to one another, each of the equal angles is right, and the straight line standing on the other is called a perpendicular to that on which it stands.

perturbed-proportion.definition: Book V: 18. A perturbed proportion arises when, there being three magnitudes and another set equal to them in multitude, as antecedent is to consequent among the first magnitudes, so is antecedent to consequent among the second magnitudes, while, as the consequent is to a third among the first magnitudes, so is a third to the antecedent among the second magnitudes.

plane.definition: Heath Greek Index: ἐπίπεδον — plane in Euclid, used for surface also in Plato and Aristotle 169

plane-angle.translation: Ἐπίπεδος δὲ γωνία ἐστὶν ἡ ἐν ἐπιπέδῳ δύο γραμμῶν ἁπτομένων ἀλλήλων κλίσις
plane-angle.definition: Book I, Def. 8: 'A plane angle is the inclination to one another of two lines in a plane which meet one another and do not lie in a straight line.'

plane-at-right-angles-to-plane.headword: plane is at right angles to a plane
plane-at-right-angles-to-plane.translation: plane at right angles to plane
plane-at-right-angles-to-plane.definition: Book XI: 4. A plane is at right angles to a plane when the straight lines drawn, in one of the planes, at right angles to the common section of the planes are at right angles to the remaining plane.

occurrences.display: plane is at right angles to a plane

plane-number.definition: Book VII: 16. And, when two numbers having multiplied one another make some number, the number so produced is called plane, and its sides are the numbers which have multiplied one another.

plane-of-reference.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Greek).

plane-surface.translation: Ἐπίπεδος ἐπιφάνειά ἐστιν, ἥτις ἐξ ἴσου ταῖς ἐφ' ἑαυτῆς εὐθείαις κεῖται
plane-surface.definition: Book I, Def. 7: 'A plane surface is a surface which lies evenly with the straight lines on itself.'

plethos-horismenon.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Greek).

plinthis.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Greek).

point.definition: Book I, Def. 1: 'A point is that which has no part.' Earlier Pythagoreans defined it as a 'monad having position' (μονὰς προσλαβοῦσα θέσιν).

polypleuron.definition: Heath Greek Index: πολύπλευρον — many-sided figure 187

porisma.definition: Heath Greek Index: πόρισμα — porism q.v.

prime-number.translation: Πρῶτος ἀριθμός ἐστιν ὁ μονάδι μόνῃ μετρούμενος
prime-number.definition: Book VII, Def. 11: 'A prime number is that which is measured by a unit alone.' (Proved infinite in multitude in IX.20).

prime-to-one-another.definition: Book VII: 12. Numbers prime to one another are those which are measured by an unit alone as a common measure.

prism.definition: Book XI: 13. A prism is a solid figure contained by planes two of which, namely those which are opposite, are equal, similar and parallel, while the rest are parallelograms.

problema.definition: Heath Greek Index: πρόβλημα — problem q.v.

promekes-arithmos.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Greek).

proportional.definition: Book V: 6. Let magnitudes which have the same ratio be called proportional.

protasis.definition: The first of the six formal divisions of a Euclidean proposition (Proclus, p. 203), stating in general terms what is given and what is sought.

pyramid.definition: Book XI: 12. A pyramid is a solid figure, contained by planes, which is constructed from one plane to one point.

quadrilateral.definition: Book I: 19. Rectilineal figures are those which are contained by straight lines, trilateral figures being those contained by three, quadrilateral those contained by four, and multilateral those contained by more than four straight lines.

quadrinomial.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Mathematical Term).

ratio.translation: Λόγος ἐστὶ δύο μεγεθῶν ὁμογενῶν ἡ κατὰ πηλικότητα ποιὰ σχέσις
ratio.definition: Book V, Def. 3: 'A ratio is a sort of relation in respect of size between two magnitudes of the same kind.' Def. 4 requires that the magnitudes, when multiplied, are capable of exceeding one another.

rational.definition: Book X, Def. 3: A straight line commensurable either in length and in square, or in square only, with the assigned straight line.

reciprocally-related.definition: Book VI: [**2.** Reciprocally related figures. *See note.*]

rectilineal-angle.definition: Book I: 9. And when the lines containing the angle are straight, the angle is called rectilineal.

rectilineal-figure.definition: Book I: 19. Rectilineal figures are those which are contained by straight lines, trilateral figures being those contained by three, quadrilateral those contained by four, and multilateral those contained by more than four straight lines.

reductio-ad-absurdum.translation: Reduction to absurdity / the impossible (ἡ εἰς τὸ ἀδύνατον ἀπαγωγή)
reductio-ad-absurdum.definition: Indirect proof establishing a truth by deducing a contradiction from the denial of the conclusion.

rhomboid.definition: Book I: 22. Of quadrilateral figures, a square is that which is both equilateral and right-angled ; an oblong that which is right-angled but not equilateral ; a rhombus that which is equilateral but not right-angled ; and a rhomboid that which has its opposite sides and angles equal to one another but is neither equilateral nor right-angled. And let quadrilaterals other than these be called trapezia.

rhombos.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Greek).

rhombus.definition: Book I: 22. Of quadrilateral figures, a square is that which is both equilateral and right-angled ; an oblong that which is right-angled but not equilateral ; a rhombus that which is equilateral but not right-angled ; and a rhomboid that which has its opposite sides and angles equal to one another but is neither equilateral nor right-angled. And let quadrilaterals other than these be called trapezia.

right-angle.definition: Book I, Def. 10: 'When a straight line set up on a straight line makes the adjacent angles equal to one another, each of the equal angles is right, and the straight line standing on the other is called a perpendicular to that on which it stands.'

right-angled.definition: Heath Greek Index: ὀρθογώνιος — right-angled: as used of quadrilaterals = rectangular 188–9

right-angled-cone.definition: Book XI: And, if the straight line which remains fixed be equal to the remaining side about the right angle which is carried round, the cone will be right-angled; if less, obtuse-angled; and if greater, acute-angled.

right-angled-triangle.definition: Book I: 21. Further, of trilateral figures, a right-angled triangle is that which has a right angle, an obtuse-angled triangle that which has an obtuse angle, and an acute-angled triangle that which has its three angles acute.

right-angles-to-plane.headword: at right angles to a plane
right-angles-to-plane.definition: Book XI: 3. A straight line is at right angles to a plane, when it makes right angles with all the straight lines which meet it and are in the plane.

occurrences.display: at right angles to a plane

scalene-triangle.definition: Book I: 20. Of trilateral figures, an equilateral triangle is that which has its three sides equal, an isosceles triangle that which has two of its sides alone equal, and a scalene triangle that which has its three sides unequal.

schema.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Greek).

schesis.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Greek).

second-apotome.definition: Book X: **2.** But if the annex be commensurable in length with the rational straight line set out, and the square on the whole be greater than that on the annex by the square on a straight line commensurable with the whole, let the apotome be called a second apotome.

second-apotome-of-a-medial-straight-line.translation: second apotome of a medial straight line
second-apotome-of-a-medial-straight-line.definition: Book X: | And let it be called a second apotome of a medial straight line. Q. E. D.

occurrences.display: second apotome of a medial straight line
second apotome of a medial straight line
second apotome of a medial straight line
second apotome of a medial straight line

second-bimedial.definition: Book X: If two medial straight lines commensurable in square only and containing a medial rectangle be added together, the whole is irrational; and let it be called a second bimedial straight line.

second-binomial.definition: Book X: **2.** but if the lesser term be commensurable in length with the rational straight line set out, let the whole be called a second binomial;

sector-of-circle.definition: Book III: 10. A sector of a circle is the figure which, when an angle is constructed at the centre of the circle, is contained by the straight lines containing the angle and the circumference cut off by them.

segment-of-circle.definition: Book III: 6. A segment of a circle is the figure contained by a straight line and a circumference of a circle.

semicircle.definition: Book I: 18. A semicircle is the figure contained by the diameter and the circumference cut off by it. And the centre of the semicircle is the same as that of the circle.

separando.translation: Separation of a ratio (antecedent − consequent to consequent)
separando.definition: Book V, Def. 15: If A : B = C : D, then separando (A − B) : B = (C − D) : D (proved in V.17).

side-of-a-medial-minus-a-medial-area.headword: ἡ μετὰ μέσου μέσον τὸ ὅλον ποιοῦσα
side-of-a-medial-minus-a-medial-area.translation: side of a medial minus a medial area
side-of-a-medial-minus-a-medial-area.definition: Book X: If from a straight line there be subtracted a straight line which is incommensurable in square with the whole and which with the whole makes the sum of the squares on them medial, twice the rectangle contained by them medial, and further the squares on them incommensurable with twice the rectangle contained by them, the remainder is irrational; and let it be called that which produces with a medial area a medial whole.

occurrences.display: ἡ μετὰ μέσου μέσον τὸ ὅλον ποιοῦσα
that which produces with a medial area a medial whole
that which produces with a medial area a medial whole

side-of-a-medial-minus-a-rational-area.headword: ἡ μετὰ ῥητοῦ μέσον τὸ ὅλον ποιοῦσα
side-of-a-medial-minus-a-rational-area.translation: side of a medial minus a rational area
side-of-a-medial-minus-a-rational-area.definition: Book X: If from a straight line there be subtracted a straight line which is incommensurable in square with the whole, and which with the whole makes the sum of the squares on them medial, but twice the rectangle contained by them rational, the remainder is irrational: and let it be called that which produces with a rational area a medial whole.

occurrences.display: ἡ μετὰ ῥητοῦ μέσον τὸ ὅλον ποιοῦσα
that which produces with a rational area a medial whole
that which produces with a rational area a medial whole

side-of-a-rational-plus-a-medial-area.translation: side of a rational plus a medial area
side-of-a-rational-plus-a-medial-area.definition: Book X: If two straight lines incommensurable in square which make the sum of the squares on them medial, but the rectangle contained by them rational, be added together, the whole straight line is irrational; and let it be called the side of a rational plus a medial area.

occurrences.display: side of a rational plus a medial area
side of a rational plus a medial area

side-of-number.definition: Book VII: 16. And, when two numbers having multiplied one another make some number, the number so produced is called plane, and its sides are the numbers which have multiplied one another.

side-of-the-sum-of-two-medial-areas.translation: side of the sum of two medial areas
side-of-the-sum-of-two-medial-areas.definition: Book X: If two straight lines incommensurable in square which make the sum of the squares on them medial, and the rectangle contained by them medial and also incommensurable with the sum of the squares on them, be added together, the whole straight line is irrational; and let it be called the side of the sum of two medial areas.

occurrences.display: side of the sum of two medial areas
side of the sum of two medial areas

similar-cones-and-cylinders.definition: Book XI: 24. Similar cones and cylinders are those in which the axes and the diameters of the bases are proportional.

similar-plane-and-solid-numbers.definition: Book VII: 21. Similar plane and solid numbers are those which have their sides proportional.

similar-rectilineal-figures.definition: Book VI: 1. Similar rectilineal figures are such as have their angles severally equal and the sides about the equal angles proportional.

similar-segments-of-circles.definition: Book III: 11. Similar segments of circles are those which admit equal angles, or in which the angles are equal to one another.

similar-solid-figures.definition: Book XI: 9. Similar solid figures are those contained by similar planes equal in multitude.

similarly-inclined-planes.definition: Book XI: 7. A plane is said to be similarly inclined to a plane as another is to another when the said angles of the inclinations are equal to one another.

sixth-apotome.definition: Book X: **6.** and, if neither, a sixth.

sixth-binomial.definition: Book X: 6. and if neither, a sixth binomial.

solid.definition: Book XI: 1. A solid is that which has length, breadth, and depth.

solid-angle.definition: Book XI: 11. A solid angle is the inclination constituted by more than two lines which meet one another and are not in the same surface, towards all the lines.

solid-number.definition: Book VII: 17. And, when three numbers having multiplied one another make some number, the number so produced is solid, and its sides are the numbers which have multiplied one another.

sphere.definition: Book XI: 14. When, the diameter of a semicircle remaining fixed, the semicircle is carried round and restored again to the same position from which it began to be moved, the figure so comprehended is a sphere.

square.definition: Book I: 22. Of quadrilateral figures, a square is that which is both equilateral and right-angled ; an oblong that which is right-angled but not equilateral ; a rhombus that which is equilateral but not right-angled ; and a rhomboid that which has its opposite sides and angles equal to one another but is neither equilateral nor right-angled. And let quadrilaterals other than these be called trapezia.

square-number.definition: Book VII: 18. A square number is equal multiplied by equal, or a number which is contained by two equal numbers.

stand-upon-circumference.definition: Book III: 9. And, when the straight lines containing the angle cut off a circumference, the angle is said to stand upon that circumference.

stoicheion.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Greek).

straight-line.translation: Εὐθεῖα γραμμή ἐστιν, ἥτις ἐξ ἴσου τοῖς ἐφ' ἑαυτῆς σημείοις κεῖται
straight-line.definition: Book I, Def. 4: 'A straight line is a line which lies evenly with the points on itself.'

surface.translation: Ἐπιφάνεια δέ ἐστιν, ὃ μῆκος καὶ πλάτος μόνον ἔχει
surface.definition: Book I, Def. 5: 'A surface is that which has length and breadth only.' Book I, Def. 6: 'The extremities of a surface are lines.'

symperasma.definition: The sixth formal division of a Euclidean proposition, reverting to the general or particular statement and closing with Q.E.D. (ὅπερ ἔδει δεῖξαι) or Q.E.F. (ὅπερ ἔδει ποιῆσαι).

synthesis.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Greek).

tangent-to-circle.definition: Book III: 2. A straight line is said to touch a circle which, meeting the circle and being produced, does not cut the circle.

tetragonismos.definition: Heath Greek Index: τετραγωνισμός — squaring, definitions of 149–50, 410

tetragonon.definition: Heath Greek Index: τετράγωνον — square: sometimes (but not in Euclid) any four-angled figure 188

theorema.definition: Heath Greek Index: θεώρημα — theorem q.v.: θεώρημα τῆς νύμφης, "Theorem of the Bride," = Eucl. I. 47, 417

theorema-tes-nymphes.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Greek).

third-apotome.definition: Book X: **3.** But if neither be commensurable in length with the rational straight line set out, and the square on the whole be greater than the square on the annex by the square on a straight line commensurable with the whole, let the apotome be called a third apotome.

third-binomial.definition: Book X: 3. and if neither of the terms be commensurable in length with the rational straight line set out, let the whole be called a third binomial.

tome.definition: Heath Greek Index: τομή — section, = point of section 170, 171, 278

topikon-theorema.definition: Heath Greek Index: τοπικὸν θεώρημα — locus-theorem 329

topos.definition: Heath Greek Index: τόπος — locus 329–31: room or space 23 n.: place (where things may be found), thus τόπος ἀναλυόμενος 8, 10: παράδοξος τόπος 329

topos-analyomenos.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Greek).

trapezion.definition: Technical geometric or mathematical term in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements (Greek).

trapezium.definition: Book I: 22. Of quadrilateral figures, a square is that which is both equilateral and right-angled ; an oblong that which is right-angled but not equilateral ; a rhombus that which is equilateral but not right-angled ; and a rhomboid that which has its opposite sides and angles equal to one another but is neither equilateral nor right-angled. And let quadrilaterals other than these be called trapezia.

trilateral.definition: Book I: 19. Rectilineal figures are those which are contained by straight lines, trilateral figures being those contained by three, quadrilateral those contained by four, and multilateral those contained by more than four straight lines.

tripleuron.definition: Heath Greek Index: τρίπλευρον — three-sided figure 187

triplicate-ratio.definition: Book V: 10. When four magnitudes are < continuously > proportional, the first is said to have to the fourth the triplicate ratio of that which it has to the second, and so on continually, whatever be the proportion.

unit.translation: Μονάς ἐστιν, καθ' ἣν ἕκαστον τῶν ὄντων ἓν λέγεται
unit.definition: Book VII, Def. 1: 'A unit is that by virtue of which each of the things that exist is called one.'
